producer: Claude implementation agent; not an independent reviewer

evidence.detail: Rows ac1/open-file-beneath (a process whose working directory is elsewhere holds an open file beneath the path: in use, the process and the file named as an open file), ac1/working-directory (at the path and beneath it; a working directory above a path is not use of it), ac1/mapped-file (a mapped file beneath the path), ac1/command-line-is-not-use (a live process whose command line names the path and a file in it: not in use), ac1/container-bind-mount (a running container with a bind mount at the path and a stopped one with a bind mount beneath it are use; a named volume, a bind mount of another path and a neighbour path are not; an engine that cannot be read is named in unread and the others are still read), ac1/clear (not in use before and after; a neighbour whose name starts the same never), ac1/helper-not-counted (corrected by the re-review: a live process is left out as a helper only when an entry pins its name, its unit and its program; a live process that names itself virtiofsd and holds a file beneath the path is counted), ac1/git-lock (git's index lock file and git's worktree lock), ac1/seam (the test seam VELDO-0300 AC1 needs), ac1/process (the kernel's start time of a live process, nothing for an ended one). Green: proof/VELDO-0299/suite-green.txt.

The rows read the real kernel process table of this host and real child processes the suite starts and ends; the container row runs the module's own client runner against a stand-in docker program first on PATH, answering the two container commands from a fixture file. No container engine was asked anything.

Falsifier space299-working-directory-only (the working directory only): ac1/open-file-beneath red, the path with an open file beneath it read not in use (ac1/mapped-file and ac1/seam red with it); noop copy green. proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

Review, fail closed. Rows closed/git-unreadable-is-locked (git refusing the worktree as dubious ownership, a client that cannot be run and a worktree whose git folder is broken, read by the real git, each give read False and locked True, and in_use is true with what git said in unread.git; a plain folder and a repository's own folder are read), closed/unnamed-process-counts (a fixture process table entry whose name cannot be read is listed in unread with its uid and the path is in use; an entry that is gone when it is read is neither a user nor unread), closed/unread-names-pids-and-uids (unread.processes is a list of {pid, uid, command, reach} in the fixture table and in this host's own table, never a count), closed/hidden-table (a table mounted hidepid=1, 2 or invisible, mounts that cannot be read and a kernel table the mounts do not name make the path in use; hidepid=0, off and no option do not).

The lead's decision, bounded fail closed. Rows reach/other-uid-shut-out-excluded (an unread process of another uid, on a path whose temporary folder is mode 700, is listed with reach None and the path is not in use; a root-owned one is judged by the mode and shut out too; the item open to all inside a closed folder is still out of reach), reach/other-uid-let-through-counted (the same processes on a folder made in a temporary place every user may pass through count, reach permissions, and the path is in use; closed to others and open to its group, a process of that group counts and one outside it does not; the owner class and the group class each decide for their own), reach/root-with-container-mount-counted (a root-owned process the mode shuts out does not count with no engine named or with a container that mounts another path; with a container whose bind mount is above the path it counts, reach container_mount, the mount is named in mounted_above and is not use by itself; so does a process of another uid, and so do both when an engine cannot be read), reach/same-uid-and-inherited (an unread process of the probing uid, one whose parent or parent's parent could reach, one whose parent the table does not show, one with no readable status and parents that lead back to themselves count; one that is shut out under a parent that is shut out does not).

Falsifiers: space299-unread-git-is-unlocked (locked no longer true when git cannot read): closed/git-unreadable-is-locked red. space299-unnamed-process-skipped (a process whose name cannot be read skipped): closed/unnamed-process-counts red. space299-every-unread-process-counts: reach/other-uid-shut-out-excluded red. space299-no-unread-process-counts: reach/other-uid-let-through-counted red. space299-container-mount-is-no-way-in: reach/root-with-container-mount-counted red. Noop copies green. proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

Re-review (verdict FIX, small), 2026-11-13. Rows on a fixture process table whose entries carry status with CapEff, loginuid, cgroup and stat as the kernel gives them: reach/root-login-counted (a root-owned process whose loginuid is set, shut out by the mode and left under a first process that is shut out, counts as privileged_login: this user's through sudo, a cron job of root's, one whose loginuid cannot be read; a root-owned one no login started and an unprivileged one are still judged by the mode), reach/capability-counted (a process that is not root with CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH or CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE in CapEff, or with capabilities that cannot be read, counts the same way; one with another capability, and a capable one no login started, do not), closed/kernel-thread-left-out (an entry whose stat carries PF_KTHREAD is in neither users nor unread; one of the same name without the flag, and one with no stat, are listed; this host's kthreadd carries the flag and is not listed), reach/container-by-its-mounts (an unread process whose cgroup names a container, under either cgroup driver's form, is judged by that container's mounts: with this user's uid number, or root with a loginuid, and a container that mounts nothing of the path, it does not count; it counts as container when no engine read holds its container or no engine is named, as container_mount when its container mounts a folder above the path, and as unknown_identity when its cgroup cannot be read; containers returns known), closed/helper-pinned (the pinned helper is not counted though its working directory is in the item; a process named virtiofsd in a session scope, in another user's manager, in a unit beneath the pinned one, with an unreadable cgroup, of another uid or run from another program is counted).

Re-review rows on this host's real process table: ac1/helper-not-counted starts a live process that writes virtiofsd into its own comm and holds a file beneath the path, and it is counted; the same live holder is left out only by an entry that pins its real name, its real unit (from /proc/<pid>/cgroup) and its real program (its exe link), and counted when the unit or the program differs or the entry is a name alone. closed/kernel-thread-left-out reads /proc/2.

Re-review falsifiers, each red on its row with the noop copy green: space299-loginuid-ignored (the loginuid not read): reach/root-login-counted. space299-capability-ignored (only uid 0 is privileged): reach/capability-counted. space299-kernel-thread-listed (the flag not read): closed/kernel-thread-left-out. space299-container-process-judged-as-host (the cgroup not read): reach/container-by-its-mounts. space299-helper-by-name-alone (a helper by its name): closed/helper-pinned and ac1/helper-not-counted. All seventeen cases of finding 299 were rerun: proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

Rows ac2/case-1-modified, ac2/case-2-staged (a staged new file; a staged rename named once), ac2/case-3-untracked (a file and a folder git does not ignore; a file it ignores is not), ac2/case-4-operation (a merge, a rebase and a cherry-pick, each stopped on a conflict, and none once given up), ac2/case-5-unlanded-commit (a commit only the worktree's own branch holds: cases [5], held by no other ref), ac2/squash-landing (after a real squash landing the trunk does not reach the tip; with no receipt it is unique work, with the receipt whose source commit is the tip it is not, another landing's receipt does not cover it, a tip that is an ancestor of the source commit is covered, a commit made after the landing is unique again, a source that is no commit id is not read), ac2/held-by-another-ref (the trunk, a tag), ac2/detached (tested on its checked-out commit against every ref), ac2/names-only (names come back, contents do not; the index and the git folder are as they were after the probe), ac2/unreadable (a folder that is no worktree, a folder inside one, an unreadable shared repository: read False and unique_work None, never no unique work). Green: proof/VELDO-0299/suite-green.txt.
The rows run the real git on repositories and worktrees the suite makes: a real squash landing on the trunk, real stopped operations (each on a real conflict), a real detached worktree.

Falsifier space299-own-branch-counted (the worktree's own branch counted among the refs that hold the commit): ac2/case-5-unlanded-commit red, the unlanded commit read no unique work (ac2/case-4-operation, ac2/squash-landing and ac2/held-by-another-ref red with it); noop green. proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

Review, fail closed. Row closed/stash-hides-unlanded-commit: a detached worktree with a commit no ref holds reads cases [5]; after a real git stash in that worktree refs/stash reaches the commit (the review's reproduction, where the probe then read no unique work) and the probe still reads cases [5], held_by empty, stashes 1; a per-worktree ref does not hold it either; the tip of a branch that a stash reaches is unique work too; a branch at the commit does hold it.
Falsifier space299-stash-holds-a-commit (every ref that reaches the commit counted, as before the review): closed/stash-hides-unlanded-commit red; noop green. proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

The review of VELDO-0300, finding 7, under the owner's rule that no work is ever lost. Row closed/personal-excludes-is-work: a worktree holding personal.txt, with HOME and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL set to a configuration whose core.excludesFile hides that file. A plain git status there prints nothing (the reviewer's reproduction, where unique_work read cases [] and untracked []); unique_work now reads untracked ['personal.txt'], case 3, unique work. The same row reads scripts/check_git_boundary.py: no git vector outside the module's _run when it is read as a funnel, the module is in FUNNELS, and read as no funnel the vector is still found, so the allowance is the only thing that passes it. Green: proof/VELDO-0299/suite-green.txt.

Falsifier space299-git-outside-the-boundary (the git arm of _run runs a plain subprocess, as before the fix): closed/personal-excludes-is-work red, the hidden file is no untracked file; noop green. All eighteen registered cases of finding 299 were rerun after the fix, each beside a copy of git_process.py (companions), each red on its row. proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

Rows ac3/branch-not-brought-across (the shared repository does not hold the agent's commit: the agent's worktree reads cases [5] and the agent repository names the branch in not_across; a tag and a second branch in the agent repository that hold the commit change nothing; the shared repository named by its work tree reads the same; cases 1 to 4 are read in the agent's worktree), ac3/brought-across (after the fetch neither has unique work, and the worktree's tip is held by the same-named branch of the shared repository), ac3/moved-on (a further commit is unique again in both while the shared repository holds the older one under the same name; a branch the shared repository holds only under another name is not across; after a second fetch neither has any). Green: proof/VELDO-0299/suite-green.txt.

The rows make an agent repository the way the sandbox's prepare does (bare, the shared store as its alternate, a linked worktree on refs/heads/agent/a1/n1) and bring the branch across the way its integrate does (a fetch of the agent's branches into the shared repository), with the real git.

Falsifier space299-agent-repository-only (the comparison made inside the agent repository only): ac3/branch-not-brought-across red, the worktree with a branch not yet brought across read no unique work (ac3/brought-across, ac3/moved-on and ac2/unreadable red with it); noop green. proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

Review, fail closed. Row closed/no-shared-repository: an agent repository holding a commit the shared repository does not, given no shared repository, is read False with unique_work None and says so (it used to compare with itself and read no unique work); a tag at a commit the shared repository does not hold is named in refs and is unique work until the branch is brought across; a stash entry of the agent repository is unique work (refs names refs/stash, stashes 1) until it is dropped, and the agent's worktree reports the stash count as a fact.

Falsifier space299-agent-repository-compares-with-itself (given no shared repository, the repository compared with itself): closed/no-shared-repository red; noop green. proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

Rows ac4/lock-held (another process holds the scratch lock: in use; the probe gave the lock back, a second launcher lock is still granted; lock held and login unsettled are both named), ac4/login-unsettled (lock free, borrow.json present and no recovery.json: in use), ac4/both-clear (lock free and journal gone, or settled into a recovery, or never borrowed: not in use; a folder that is gone or is a link is held by no lock), ac4/journal-root (with no root given the journal is looked for under XDG_STATE_HOME/veldo/borrowed-logins, the launcher's own place). Green: proof/VELDO-0299/suite-green.txt.

The lock row's holder is a real child process that takes the shared lock on the scratch folder exactly as the launcher does (agent_sandbox.py:2208-2209); the journal is real files in a fixture journal root shaped as the launcher's (borrow.json, recovery.json).

Falsifier space299-lock-only (the lock only): ac4/login-unsettled red, the scratch with a free lock and an unsettled login read not in use (ac4/journal-root red with it); noop green. proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

Review, fail closed. Row closed/scratch-unopenable-is-locked: a scratch folder that cannot be opened (a name no folder can have, and, run as a user other than root, a folder of mode 000) reads lock_held True, read False, in use; a journal that cannot be looked into reads login_unsettled True, read False, in use; the scratch that can be opened is read and not in use.
Falsifier space299-unopenable-scratch-is-unlocked (a folder that cannot be opened read as not locked): closed/scratch-unopenable-is-locked red; noop green. proof/VELDO-0299/mutations.txt.

checks.name: unit
checks.command: python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 136_veldo_0299_space_probe (46 rows, 72 checks). After the fix for the review of VELDO-0300 every space suite was rerun green, each on its own: 130 (48 checks), 131 (40), 132 (57), 133 (56), 134 (42), 135 (150), 136 (72), 137 (49), 138 (55).

checks.name: fast checks
checks.command: bash scripts/check_template_sync.sh; bash scripts/check_docs.sh; bash scripts/check_generated.sh; bash scripts/check_lint.sh; python3 scripts/check_personal_setup.py; python3 scripts/update_index.py; python3 .veldo/validate.py spec on the spec and all, exit 0. After the fix for the review of VELDO-0300: python3 scripts/check_git_boundary.py passes for the whole tree.

checks.name: gate
checks.reason: The build, the review fix and the re-review fix ran single suites and fast checks only, as instructed. The lead runs ./scripts/verify.sh through the gate lock; the eighteen registered teeth cases (finding 299) were run here through the driver's own materialize() and worker(), not through the teeth run.

assumptions: The probes are functions of engine/.veldo/control_space_probe.py: process, processes, reach, containers, git_lock, worktrees, in_use, scratch, unique_work, agent_repository (and located, repository, protected from VELDO-0330). Each returns facts; none defers or removes. The rules that read them are VELDO-0330; the removers are VELDO-0300.

Not directly proven against a real container engine: the docker client's answers are a stand-in program's (container ls with all, quiet and no-trunc; container inspect with Id, Name, State.Status and Mounts of Type, Source, Destination). The design leaves the check of both engines to the Docker tickets (0306, 0307). A desktop engine that reports a bind source under another prefix than the host path would not match; not measured here.

[Superseded by the re-review of 2026-11-13; see the last assumptions.] The file-sharing helper is recognised by its command name, HELPERS = ('virtiofsd',), the helper seen on this host's desktop engine; the list is a parameter. Whether other desktop engines need other names is not measured.

git holds a lock on the worktree is read as: a lock file (index.lock, HEAD.lock, config.lock, shallow.lock) in the worktree's own git folder, or git's worktree lock. The design does not say which; both are returned apart. No acceptance criterion names it; the row ac1/git-lock covers it.

unique_work takes the landed source commits as an argument (landed): the caller reads the completion receipts' source field (control_landing.py SUBJECT_FIELDS) and this module opens no store. The row's receipts are fixture records of that shape. A source that is not a full commit id is not read.

Case 5 tests the checked-out commit, as the design allows (the branch tip is the checked-out commit). For a worktree of the shared repository every ref of that repository other than the worktree's own branch counts, remote-tracking refs and tags included: the design says no ref other than that branch itself. The trunk is one of those refs and is not named apart.

For an agent's worktree only the shared repository's refs and the landed source commits count; refs of the agent repository never do. For the agent repository a branch is across when the shared repository's branch of the same name reaches its commit.

Case 3 lists an untracked folder as one name, as git's normal untracked listing does, and each case names at most 20 paths with the rest counted in more. The review-scratch exception of case 3 is the rule's: the probe returns cases and the rule leaves 3 out for a review worktree.
The operations of case 4 are the three the design names and two more of the same family that git marks the same way: a revert and a stopped sequence of picks.

The scratch lock is tested as the launcher's own stale pass tests it (agent_sandbox.py:2101): an exclusive lock asked for without waiting and given back at once. For that instant a launcher that asked for its shared lock on the same folder would be refused; the launcher locks a folder it has just made, which no item names yet. The unsettled test is the launcher's pending_borrow (agent_sandbox.py:1986-1990), copied and not imported, since the launcher is a protected script and this module is standard library only.

SEAM['after_in_use'] is the probe's test seam that VELDO-0300 AC1 names. process(pid) is the fact rule 3 needs for a session's recorded process (id and start time, design 4.1); the rest of rule 3 reads the store and is not a probe.
The spec's own History and specs/index.md are not changed, as in VELDO-0298. docs are not changed: documents for space management are VELDO-0322.

Review (verdict FIX), 2026-11-13, the lead's rule: every probe fails closed. in_use is now true when a user was seen (found) or when something unread could hold the path (unknown): an unread process with a reach, a hidden process table, an unread engine, a worktree git cannot read. The AC1 rows that read the host's own process table assert found, not in_use, because on this host unreadable processes of the probing user make in_use true for every path.

Only a branch, a tag and a remote-tracking ref hold a commit (HOLDING_REFS). A stash, git's per-worktree refs and every other ref do not. stashes is reported by unique_work as a fact and is no case of rule 5: a stash of the shared repository outlives the worktree. For an agent repository a stash entry is unique work, because the repository's stashes go with it; that reading is the builder's, from the lead's rule that what cannot be decided is unique work.

git_lock tells apart no git at all (git says not a git repository and the folder holds no .git entry: read, no lock), inside a worktree and not its top (read, no lock), a worktree's top or a repository's own folder (its lock files are looked for), and everything else (read False, locked True).

[Superseded by the re-review of 2026-11-13; see the last assumptions.] Bounded fail closed is the lead's decision as recorded in design section 7. Two things in it are the builder's reading and are for the lead to confirm. (1) A root-owned process is judged by the owner, group and mode of the directories like any other uid, never by its privilege, and is excluded only where the mode shuts uid 0 out and no container has a bind mount at, beneath or above the path; the lead's words were that root is excluded only for paths no container mounts and only when the path's directories deny root nothing special. (2) A container mount at, beneath or above the path, or an unread engine, makes every unread process count, not only root's, and a process whose parent could reach counts; both go further than the lead's words, in the closed direction.

Not seen by the bound: a process of another uid that kept a working directory or a descriptor from a parent that could reach the path, after every such parent ended. A directory with an access list is not judged and counts as special; no row makes a real access list, because the suite has no tool to set one.

Measured on this host, 2026-11-13, for an item under the owner's home folder (mode 750), both engines named: 536 unread processes, 527 excluded, 9 counted: six of the probing user's own that are not dumpable (the systemd user manager, its PAM helper, two of the desktop engine's backend, ssh-agent, one short-lived command) and three that the home folder's group lets through. So such an item still reads in use here. Not a test: a measurement, recorded in the design as the lead's open point.

[Superseded by the re-review of 2026-11-13; see the last assumptions.] Not changed: the review's low findings 8a (the helper is matched by its command name), 8b (the exclusive lock test can refuse a launcher starting at that instant), 8c (the calling process is not excluded) and 8d (volumes with a bind option). No row runs against a real container engine; the review read both of this host's engines by hand.
The spec's History has the review's lines; specs/index.md regenerated with no change.

Re-review, 2026-11-13. HELPERS is a list of identities, measured on this host's desktop engine: name virtiofsd, exe /opt/docker-desktop/bin/virtiofsd, cgroup /user.slice/user-{uid}.slice/user@{uid}.service/app.slice/docker-desktop.service. A process is a helper only with that name, the probing uid, exactly that unit and, when its exe link can be read, that program; an exe link that cannot be read does not disqualify it (the re-review asks for the exe of a readable process). Another install path or unit name needs another entry; the list is a parameter. This closes the first review's 8a. 8b, 8c and 8d are not changed.

Re-review, root and capabilities. privileged is uid 0 (the uid the kernel checks a path against) or CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE or CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH in CapEff of the status file; a status with no readable CapEff is privileged. A privileged process counts as privileged_login when /proc/<pid>/loginuid holds anything but 4294967295 or cannot be read. On a kernel built without audit there is no loginuid file, so every privileged process counts and every item is deferred there; not measured. A privileged process whose loginuid is unset is judged by the mode: a stated policy for system daemons (the docstring and design section 7 say so), not a reading. Residual, named in the design: a system service no login started that is configured to work in the path.

Re-review, containers. A process is in a container when its cgroup file holds an id of 64 hexadecimal digits (the systemd driver's docker-<id>.scope and the cgroupfs driver's /docker/<id> are the rows; any other runtime's id of that shape is read the same way). It is then judged before its uid: by container_mount when a mount is a way to the path, else not at all when an engine that was read holds the id, else as container. The builder's reading, for the lead to confirm: (1) a process of a container no named engine holds counts, so an installation that names no engine on a host that runs containers defers every item (169 such processes on this host); (2) when any container's mount is a way to the path every unread process counts, as before, including a process of a container that mounts nothing of it; (3) a process whose cgroup file cannot be read counts as unknown_identity. Containers of a desktop engine run in its virtual machine and are not in the host's table.

Re-review, kernel threads. A process whose stat flags carry PF_KTHREAD (0x00200000) is left out of users and of unread before anything else of it is read; a stat that cannot be read leaves nothing out.

Not built, by the lead's instruction: the owner-approved list of process names and the narrow capability reader. The lead decides between them with the owner. Until then the user's own undumpable processes count as same_uid. Measured on this host, 2026-11-13, for an item under the owner's home folder with both engines named: 355 unread listed, 347 excluded, 8 counted: five of the user's own (the systemd user manager, its PAM helper, two of the desktop engine's backend, ssh-agent) and three root-owned whose loginuid is the user's (a session worker, two mount helpers). So every such item is still in use here. The earlier measurement's sixth same-uid process was a container's health check, not the user's; the design's paragraph is corrected.
nested(path, skip) is added to this module for VELDO-0330's rule 6 and is proven there (suite 137, ac1/nested-repository-holds-worktree). It reads names only: os.scandir, no git, no link followed.
The spec's History has the re-review's line; specs/index.md regenerated with no change.

The review of VELDO-0300, finding 7: git is run through the one Git boundary (git_process.py beside the module, isolated profile), so the module is no longer standard library only in the strict sense: it loads that one sibling by its own path. --no-optional-locks stands for GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, which the boundary would strip. A runner a caller gives is handed the vector as it is; the default runner and the removers' runner send it through the boundary. scripts/check_git_boundary.py was changed to allow the module as a funnel; it is not a protected path. commit and tree above still name the earlier build; this fix is the commit that carries this bundle.
rollback: Revert the change. Nothing is removed by this ticket, so nothing on disk changes.
